title: Pilot quality retro & guardrail audit - Zenith Care weekly sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review recent evals on clinical summarization pilot; identified a regression in hallucination rate after prompt set change; discussed guardrail tightening, prompt rollback vs prompt surgery, scoring thresholds, and short A/B for quantized vs fp16 model variant. Agreed next steps: Redwood to push updated prompt set and run 5k eval, customer to provide 50 failure examples, schedule benchmarking run in 5 days.
topics: evaluation results, prompt set changes, hallucination regression, guardrails (dosage safety), scoring metrics (exact match, pass rate), A/B plan, rollout criteria, infra notes (VPC logs, KV cache behavior)
next_steps: Redwood (Priya) to push prompt patch clinical_summaries_v3b and run a 5k batch eval by 2025-12-08
Zenith (Maya) to upload 50 flagged failures to shared folder and mark severity by 2025-12-05
Schedule dedicated benchmarking run (GPUs) for quantized vs fp16—Avery to propose slots 2025-12-09 or 2025-12-10
Redwood to share guardrail rule snapshot and match for med-dosage checks before next demo
action_items: Priya Nair: patch prompts (clinical_summaries_v3b) and kick off eval; due 2025-12-08
Maya Ruiz: export 50 failure cases + severity labels to /zenith/shared/pilot-failures; due 2025-12-05
Avery Chen: send pricing delta for dedicated capacity test run and include estimated token cost; due 2025-12-06
Samir Patel: confirm stakeholder availability for go/no-go on 2025-12-11 presentation; due 2025-12-07
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 mins
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neal (Zenith Head of AI), Maya Ruiz (ML Engineer), Samir Patel (Product)

[00:00] Avery: okay hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll keep to 45 minutes. quick agenda: eval readout, regressions, prompt surgery options, guardrail changes, and next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Liam: yep that works, thanks. excited to see the numbers.
[00:25] Priya: i'll start with the summary of the run we did last night — this was the 10k batch eval on clinical_summaries_v3 using Redwood hosted fp16 variant + prefix KV caching enabled. overall exact match went up 2 points, but hallucination flags ticked up on medication dosage items.
[00:47] Maya: can you unpack the hallucination flags? is this hallucinating new meds or wrong dosages?
[00:54] Priya: mostly dosage; there were about 42 cases where the model inferred a dosage (e.g., '50 mg' vs '5 mg'), sometimes adding units when they weren't in the note. the safety rule we have flags when dosage appears that wasn't in source or is outside of plausible range.
[01:15] Samir: that's the one showstopper for us — if it makes the wrong dosage we can't ship.
[01:22] Avery: agreed — this is why our guardrails are prioritized. quick question, did the regression coincide with the prompt set change last week?
[01:31] Priya: yes we swapped clinical_summaries_v3 -> v3a which added a short instruction asking the model to 'fill inferred values when context suggests', which in hindsight encouraged overconfident fills.
[01:45] Liam: so prompt cause seems likely. what about model variant? any difference between quantized run and fp16?
[01:53] Priya: we did a small A/B (2k each) — quantized had slightly lower hallucination but worse verbatim exact match. not conclusive; need a larger run. also note that the KV cache interaction changed prompt truncation in some long notes which might alter context window.
[02:17] Maya: hmm truncation could lose explicit dosage lines earlier in the note. can we increase prefix retention?
[02:24] Priya: yes, we can tune cache window or bump sequence length for these longer examples; tradeoff is latency and token cost.
[02:33] Samir: what's the expected latency delta if we increase seq length? ballpark numbers please.
[02:39] Priya: on Dedicated it's about +12–18ms p95 for these flows; on hosted it can be +25–40ms depending on batching. we'll give a more precise table after the dedicated bench.
[02:52] Avery: let's go through a couple of example failures. Maya, did you bring the 8 flagged ones you mentioned in your note?
[03:00] Maya: yep i uploaded a short set to the shared folder — examples zc-045 through zc-052. they're annotated with severity (critical/high/medium).
[03:11] Priya: looking at zc-047, model inferred 'Metformin 500 mg' when the source said 'Metformin' with no dose. probably because prompt encouraged filling. we could do two things: revert the fill instruction, or add a guardrail that suppresses dosage hallucination unless exact match present.
[03:36] Liam: which approach has lower risk for regressions in other metrics?
[03:41] Priya: reverting prompt is fastest and lowest risk — it brought exact match down earlier but reduced hallucination. guardrail is safer long term because it's rule-based and can be tuned for edge cases. ideally we do both: immediate rollback + parallel guardrail engineering.
[03:57] Avery: that matches what we usually recommend. for the pilot timeline — do you want a hotfix rollback now, or wait until after the bigger 5k eval?
[04:06] Samir: i'd prefer rollback now for any production-looking paths. the pilot is getting internal users.
[04:12] Liam: agreed rollback now, but we still need the 5k to validate other metrics.
[04:17] Priya: okay i'll patch clinical_summaries_v3b which removes the 'fill inferred values' line and keep the rest of the prompt identical. we'll push it to the pilot env and re-run a 5k eval.
[04:28] Maya: and can you add an explicit guardrail rule: if a dosage value is not lexically present in the source, the model must return 'dosage: unknown' or empty, rather than fabricating?
[04:37] Priya: yes, we can add that to the post-processing sanitizer; it's a quick change but we should test for false negatives.
[04:44] Avery: on scoring — currently your test harness uses 'exact match' and a manual labeler pass rate. any interest in adding a hallucination score or confidence threshold?
[04:55] Liam: yes, we'd like an automated hallucination score wired into alerts. what's the false positive rate like?
[04:59] Priya: in our last runs, an automated hallucination classifier had ~8% false positives, but with threshold tuning and the sanitizer we can get it to ~3–4% while catching 85% of true hallucinations.
[05:12] Samir: can you surface that metric in the Redwood Console? like a per-batch hallucination_rate and a trendline?
[05:18] Avery: absolutely — console can show per-model, per-prompt-set trendlines, and we'll add a custom tile for hallucination_rate and severity breakdown.
[05:26] Maya: quick infra question — are the audit logs for the private pilot accessible in the VPC? we need them for our compliance team.
[05:33] Priya: yes, audit logs are forwarded to your Splunk instance via the VPC connector; we also keep a hashed token-level trace in the control plane for 30 days by default.
[05:41] Liam: make sure PHI is never in the control plane logs — remember earlier compliance note.
[05:45] Avery: noted — we will redact PHI before it leaves the VPC.
[05:49] Priya: also, for the KV cache behavior — i dug into the cache policy: it was evicting earlier due to small default window; i'll increase retention for tests so truncation is less likely. that's a config change, no infra redeploy needed.
[06:00] Samir: what about rolling to dedicated for the benchmarking run? cost implications?
[06:06] Avery: for a short dedicated bench (1–2 hours) we can spin up a small reserved pool — we'll estimate token & infra delta after we know sequence lengths and batch shapes. i'll include a pricing delta in an email.
[06:18] Priya: back to the eval: suggested pass criteria for go/no-go — hallucination_rate < 0.5% critical, labeler pass_rate >= 92%, exact_match >= baseline - 1.5 points. open to adjusting these thresholds.
[06:34] Liam: those seem reasonable; i'd also add 'no critical safety failures in top 10k'.
[06:40] Maya: agreed. and let's capture the regression windows so we can do root cause later.
[06:45] Priya: we'll keep a changelog entry.
[06:48] Avery: anything on prompt instrumentation? can we include a prompt diff in the console?
[06:53] Priya: we have a prompt versioning view — i'll attach the diff for v3->v3a->v3b in the shared notes link.
[07:00] (brief cross-talk about link names and folder paths)
[07:12] Liam: on the A/B for quantized vs fp16: how many tokens do you need to make it statistically meaningful?
[07:18] Priya: for the hallucination metric we're targeting, i recommend 5k per arm to get stable estimates; if you care about rare critical failures, increase to 10k.
[07:27] Samir: budget-wise let's do 5k per arm and then do the 10k for the final run if needed.
[07:33] Maya: note — i'll add a list of edge-case families (long notes, scanned OCR artifacts, shorthand med entries) to the shared doc.
[07:41] Priya: perfect, that helps with stratified sampling.
[07:45] Avery: any competitors or different approaches you've looked at since last sync?
[07:49] Liam: we're watching Anthropic's safety features and also did a short eval against an internal fine-tuned baseline. but infra and cost tradeoffs keep leaning us to Redwood because of the unified rollout tools.
[08:01] Priya: quick ops note — we'll make sure the rollback doesn't auto-affect other clients; it'll be scoped to your pilot route.
[08:07] Maya: perfect.
[08:09] (silence as people scan the shared examples)
[08:25] Avery: to recap: Priya will patch prompts (v3b) and add sanitizer guardrail; run 5k eval; Maya will upload 50 failure cases; Avery to send pricing delta and propose bench windows; we'll add console tiles for hallucination_rate. next sync after eval results — propose 2025-12-11 at 14:00 UTC.
[08:45] Liam: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:48] Priya: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels and filler; timestamps are approximate. Links referenced: shared folder /zenith/shared/pilot-failures, prompt diffs in /redwood/prompt-diffs/zenith/clinical_summaries.
questions: Can we rollback prompt quickly? How to tune KV cache to avoid truncation? What's acceptable hallucination threshold for go/no-go?
